<role>
You write a one-page opportunity brief for a Keelwater product manager. Keelwater makes claims-handling software. You use only the facts and customer insights below.
</role>
<opportunity>
{
 "title": "Checkbox requirement causes user lockouts",
 "problem_statement": "Handlers are frequently locked out of the system because they miss a confusing checkbox requirement. This prevents them from processing claims and disrupts their workflow."
}
</opportunity>
<fact_sheet>
{
 "as_of": "2026-11-03",
 "accounts_n": 1,
 "mentions_n": 1,
 "routes_n": 1,
 "mentions_by_route": {
  "support": 1
 },
 "arr_total_gbp": 250000.0,
 "renewals_90d_n": 1,
 "accounts": [
  {
   "name": "Ashcombe Property Mutual",
   "arr_gbp": 250000.0,
   "renewal_date": "2026-11-30",
   "mentions": 1
  }
 ]
}
</fact_sheet>
<insights>
[
 {
  "id": "b6f375d94687aa05",
  "quote": "we’ve had two handlers locked out already this week just from missing a checkbox.",
  "account": "Ashcombe Property Mutual",
  "route": "support",
  "date": "2026-10-25T14:19:00+00:00"
 }
]
</insights>
<rules>
- Cite every insight you rely on as [i:INSIGHT_ID], using the id exactly as given. Cite at least three different insights when three or more are given, and cover every route that appears.
- Use these sections, in this order, as Markdown headings: "## Problem", "## Who is affected", "## Evidence", "## Why now".
- Every bullet under "Who is affected" and "Evidence" ends with a citation. Every sentence that contains a number or a date carries a citation.
- Copy every account count, mention count, route count, renewal count and ARR figure from the fact sheet. Never compute, add up or round a number yourself; write an ARR figure only as it appears in the fact sheet, in pounds.
- Write counts as digits exactly as the fact sheet gives them ("5 accounts", never "five accounts"); never write "one customer" or "a single customer" unless the fact sheet count says 1 for that same thing.
- Put text in quotation marks only when it is a customer quote copied word for word, character for character, from one insight cited in the same sentence. Never put quotation marks around a paraphrase, a fragment of your own wording or a phrase from the fact sheet; when unsure, paraphrase without quotation marks.
- Name a customer only when a cited insight in the same sentence belongs to that customer.
- Do not claim more than the evidence shows: no "all customers", no scope wider than the cited accounts, and mention any cited insight that points the other way.
- Do not recommend a solution.
</rules>
<output>
JSON only: {"body_md": the brief as Markdown, "citations": the list of insight ids you cited}
</output>

{"body_md": "## Problem

Handlers are frequently locked out of the system because they miss a confusing checkbox requirement. This prevents them from processing claims and disrupts their workflow.

## Who is affected

- Handlers at Ashcombe Property Mutual, where 1 mention of this issue has been logged via the support route [i:b6f375d94687aa05].
- The account carries 250000.0 in ARR and has a renewal date of 2026-11-30, with 1 renewal falling within the next 90 days [i:b6f375d94687aa05].

## Evidence

- Across 1 accounts and 1 mentions, the only route represented is support, with 1 mention on that route [i:b6f375d94687aa05].
- Ashcombe Property Mutual reported: "we’ve had two handlers locked out already this week just from missing a checkbox." [i:b6f375d94687aa05]
- The insight was logged on 2026-10-25 [i:b6f375d94687aa05].

## Why now

- The fact sheet is current as of 2026-11-03, and the affected account renews on 2026-11-30, which is 1 renewal within 90 days [i:b6f375d94687aa05].
- The lockouts described are recurring within a single week, indicating the checkbox requirement is actively disrupting claim processing at this account [i:b6f375d94687aa05].
", "citations": ["b6f375d94687aa05"]}
